## Moist adiabat extrapolation with the effective heat capacity (`extrapolate_dlnp`, `extrapolate_dz`) {#sec-ch03-adiabat}

### Summary

An initial atmosphere is often built by lifting a parcel along an adiabat: entropy is held fixed while pressure
falls, and condensates form when vapours saturate. `ThermoX` provides this step. Given $(T, p, x)$ at one level,
`extrapolate_dlnp` moves to a new pressure and `extrapolate_dz` to a new height under hydrostatic balance, and both
return the temperature and equilibrated composition there. The temperature is found by a Newton iteration whose
slope is the effective heat capacity, the ordinary heat capacity plus the latent heat released per kelvin by
condensation that keeps the parcel saturated. This follows the multi-condensable moist adiabat of Li, Ingersoll and Oyafuso (2018,
[doi:10.1175/JAS-D-17-0257.1](https://doi.org/10.1175/JAS-D-17-0257.1)).

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Hold the molar entropy at its target, @eq-ch03-adiabat-target, using the slope
@eq-ch03-adiabat-cpeff.

**Data.** $T$ [K], $p$ [Pa], $x_n$ [-] in and out (overwritten); $\Delta \ln p$ [-] or $\Delta z$ [m] and $g$
[m s$^{-2}$].

**Placement.** API calls, typically one per level when building a column.

**Activation.** `extrapolate_dlnp(temp, pres, xfrac, dlnp, ...)`, `extrapolate_dz(temp, pres, xfrac, dz, grav,
...)`; `rainout` default off.

**Guarantee / limits.** In $\ln p$, no step error: entropy is held to 10 times `ftol`. In $z$, trapezoidal
hydrostatics.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $\bar s$, entropy per mole of mixture, gas and condensate [J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$]; $\bar c_p$, frozen
heat capacity per mole of mixture [J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$]; $\bar c_p^{\mathrm{eff}}$, effective heat capacity per
mole of mixture [J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$]; $\xi_r$, extent of reaction $r$ per mole of mixture [-]; $\mathsf G$, the
gain matrix of the saturation adjustment at fixed $T$ and $p$ (@sec-ch04) [-]; $\Delta h_r = \sum_n \nu_{nr} h_n$
[J mol$^{-1}$]; $\bar\mu$, mean molar mass of the mixture [kg mol$^{-1}$]; $g$, gravitational acceleration,
positive [m s$^{-2}$]; $\Delta z$, height change, positive upward [m]; $\nu_{nr}$ and $c_{p,n}$ as in
@sec-ch03-species-functions. Symbols of the notation table (@sec-appa): $K_r$, $h_n$, $x_n$, $c_n$, $x_{\mathrm g}$, $N_{\mathrm g}$.

### Derivation

**Effective heat capacity.** Hold $p$ fixed and let $T$ change by $\mathrm d T$ in a saturated parcel. The frozen
part of the enthalpy change per mole of mixture is $\bar c_p\, \mathrm d T$ with $\bar c_p = \sum_n x_n c_{p,n}$.
The reaction extents change too, by $\mathrm d \xi_r$, releasing $-\Delta h_r\, \mathrm d \xi_r$. Saturation is
kept: each active reaction's log quotient, formed from the gas mole fractions $x_n / x_{\mathrm g}$ with sums over
gases only (@sec-ch04), follows its log saturation constant at fixed $p$, so with $\mathsf G$ the derivative of
the log quotients with respect to the extents,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf G\, \frac{\mathrm d \boldsymbol\xi}{\mathrm d T} &= \frac{\mathrm d \ln \mathbf K}{\mathrm d T}, \\
\bar c_p^{\mathrm{eff}} &= \sum_n x_n c_{p,n} + \sum_r \Delta h_r \frac{\mathrm d \xi_r}{\mathrm d T} .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-adiabat-cpeff}

@eq-ch03-adiabat-cpeff is computed in `effective_cp`
({{< code src/thermo/extrapolate_ad.cpp ThermoXImpl::effective_cp >}}). Before solving the first line, the code
divides each row of $\mathsf G$ and of the right side by that row's largest magnitude, which leaves the solution
unchanged in exact arithmetic and lowers the condition number. The solve is a least-squares solve (`gelsd`) on CPU
and a pseudo-inverse with absolute tolerance $10^{-6}$ on CUDA. Inactive reactions have zero rows and get zero
$\mathrm d\xi_r/\mathrm d T$. Without a gain matrix (no reactions) the function returns $\bar c_p$.

**Entropy target.** The parcel's molar entropy is $\bar s = S / \sum_n c_n$, with $S$ of
@eq-ch03-thermo-x-totals. A reversible step keeps $\bar s$; a user-supplied rate adds a prescribed change:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\bar s_{\mathrm{target}} &= \bar s_0 + \frac{\mathrm d \bar s}{\mathrm d \ln p}\, \Delta \ln p , \\
\bar s_{\mathrm{target}} &= \bar s_0 + \frac{\mathrm d \bar s}{\mathrm d z}\, \Delta z ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-adiabat-target}

the first line for `extrapolate_dlnp` and the second for `extrapolate_dz`, with the rates the arguments `ds_dlnp`
and `ds_dz` (default 0). Both functions compute their target at entry.

**Temperature update in $\ln p$.** At the new pressure, $\partial \bar s / \partial T = \bar c_p^{\mathrm{eff}} / T$
along the saturated path, so Newton's method gives

$$
T \leftarrow T \left(1 + \frac{\bar s_{\mathrm{target}} - \bar s(T)}{\bar c_p^{\mathrm{eff}}}\right) ,
$$

computed in `extrapolate_dlnp` ({{< code src/thermo/extrapolate_ad.cpp ThermoXImpl::extrapolate_dlnp >}}).

**Hydrostatic step in $z$.** For a step $\Delta z$, the pressure follows the trapezoidal rule of
$\mathrm d p / \mathrm d z = -\rho g$:

$$
p_1 = p_0 - \tfrac12 (\rho_0 + \rho_1)\, g\, \Delta z .
$$ {#eq-ch03-adiabat-hydrostatic}

The temperature update adds the change of $\bar s$ caused by the pressure change of this iteration,
$-x_{\mathrm g} \mathcal R\, \Delta \ln p$ for ideal gases, with $x_{\mathrm g}$ of @sec-ch03-eos:

$$
T \leftarrow T \left(1 + \frac{\bar s_{\mathrm{target}} - \bar s + x_{\mathrm g} \mathcal R\, \Delta \ln p}
{\bar c_p^{\mathrm{eff}}}\right) .
$$

The first pressure guess is isothermal, $p = p_0 \exp(-g \bar\mu \Delta z / (\mathcal R T))$. Both updates are in
`extrapolate_dz` ({{< code src/thermo/extrapolate_ad.cpp ThermoXImpl::extrapolate_dz >}}).

**Pseudo-adiabat.** With `rainout`, the condensate formed in the step leaves the parcel and carries its entropy
with it. Per mole of the conserved dry gas, the target becomes

$$
\bar s_{\mathrm{target}} = \frac{x_0^{\mathrm{new}}}{x_0^{\mathrm{old}}}\, \bar s_0
- \frac{\sum_{m \ge N_{\mathrm g}} s_m c_m}{\sum_{n < N_{\mathrm g}} c_n} + (\text{prescribed change}) ,
$$

with $s_m$ the condensate entropy of @eq-ch03-species-functions-scond, and the condensate mole fractions are set to
zero and the rest renormalised.

What is exact and what is truncated: `extrapolate_dlnp` has no truncation error in $\Delta \ln p$; its end state
satisfies $\bar s(T, p_1) = \bar s_{\mathrm{target}}$ to within 10 times `ftol`, in J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$, whatever the
step. `extrapolate_dz` adds the trapezoidal error of @eq-ch03-adiabat-hydrostatic, second order in $\Delta z$ for a
smooth $\rho(z)$ (a standard property of the trapezoidal rule; no test measures it). The executable check is not written yet.

### Numerical method

Each call runs a fixed-point loop of at most `max_iter` iterations. In every iteration it: (1) resets $x$ to the
input composition; (2) runs the saturation adjustment `forward` at the current $(T, p)$, which returns $\mathsf G$;
(3) with `rainout`, forms the pseudo-adiabatic target and removes the condensates; (4) evaluates
$\bar c_p^{\mathrm{eff}}$ and $\bar s$; (5) stops if $\max \lvert \bar s_{\mathrm{target}} - \bar s \rvert$ is below 10 times `ftol`;
(6) updates $T$ (and, in `extrapolate_dz`, first $p$). The convergence test is a maximum over all cells. If the loop
ends without meeting it, a warning is printed and the last iterate is returned.

The adiabat figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

: Code map of the adiabat extrapolation. {#tbl-ch03-adiabat-code}

Warnings a user can hit: "extrapolate_dlnp does not converge after N iterations" and "extrapolate_ad does not
converge after N iterations" (the second is printed by `extrapolate_dz`). The `verbose` option prints the state of
every iteration. Both functions overwrite `temp`, `pres` and `xfrac` in place.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_thermo.release` (`DeviceTest.extrapolate_ad`) | molar entropy unchanged after a step $\Delta \ln p = -0.1$ | $10^{-3}$ rel. and abs. | not yet derived |
| `test_earth.py` | a 2-D column built by `extrapolate_dlnp` runs | none | smoke test, no assertion |

: Tests of the adiabat extrapolation. {#tbl-ch03-adiabat-tests}

`DeviceTest.extrapolate_ad` is skipped in float32 and runs in float64 on CPU and on CUDA when a GPU is present.
`tests/test_effective_cp_heap_state.py` asserts that `effective_cp` on CPU gives one value whatever the heap holds
and keeps the latent term, but it is not registered with ctest at the pin, so CI does not run it.
`test_jupiter_tp_adiabat.py` builds a deep adiabat with repeated `forward` calls and its own temperature bracket; it
does not call `extrapolate_dlnp` or `extrapolate_dz`, so it is not evidence for this section. No test covers
`extrapolate_dz`, `rainout`, or the trapezoidal order: missing evidence.

### Limits

`extrapolate_dz` and `rainout` are untested. The CUDA path of `effective_cp` uses an absolute pseudo-inverse
tolerance of $10^{-6}$ on the row-scaled matrix, while the CPU path uses `gelsd`; whether the two agree on
ill-conditioned gain matrices is not measured. The entropy target uses the constant-$c_p$ gas entropy of
@sec-ch03-species-functions, so with `use-nasa9-cp` the step conserves that entropy, not the NASA-9 one (verified by
reading `eval_entropy_R`; the size of the effect is not measured).
